key_insight: A local, geometry-based ghost-node wetting condition lets a conservative Allen–Cahn lattice Boltzmann model impose accurate contact angles while keeping the solver scalable and thread-safe.
engineering_relevance: This enables reliable simulation of wetted multiphase flows in complex geometries, supporting design and analysis of droplets, impacts, and gravity-driven transport in porous or sharp-edged devices.
method: Reconstruct the wall normal locally and set ghost phase-field values to impose the target contact angle.
Use donor-fluid extrapolation for the wetting update, keeping the boundary treatment fully local.
Apply a separate global volume correction to control phase-field mass conservation.
evidence_signal: The method was validated on static contact-angle cases, short-time spreading, hydrophobic impact, and gravity-driven orifice flow, matching imposed angles and classical scaling laws.
watch_item: Because mass control is handled by a separate global correction, large or highly transient simulations may need careful tuning to avoid unintended coupling with the wetting boundary update.
paper_title: Accurate wetting dynamics via a conservative Allen-Cahn based lattice Boltzmann approach for multiphase flows
